title: Runtime kernel compatibility shim and staged v3 rollout to mitigate startup regression
creator: Amina Patel
description:
Summary: After integrating FlashAttention v3 variants into the runtime kernel pool, several workloads showed intermittent increases in first-token latency and occasional OOM near startup on long-sequence workloads. This ticket implements a compatibility shim that coordinates kernel selection, non-blocking micro-warmup, and fallback logic to v2 kernels while we gather telemetry and tune v3 parameters. The goal is to restore predictable startup latency and memory behavior without blocking the v3 rollout.

Background: v3 kernels offer throughput and memory benefits for steady-state decode but introduce sensitivity at startup due to different workspace sizing and tiling heuristics. We observed: (1) spike in 95th/99th first-token latency for batches with cold KV cache, (2) rare workspace allocation failures on GPUs with memory fragmentation, and (3) higher variance in per-head microbatching heuristics.

Scope: Implement a runtime-side shim that: (a) probes candidate kernel variants with a lightweight microbench per GPU at allocation time; (b) places v3 kernels behind a staged canary gate that requires microbench success and output-stability checks; (c) performs a brief, non-blocking warmup sequence to populate KV caches and smooth allocator behavior; (d) falls back to v2 kernels for the first N requests or until a health criteria is met; (e) emits detailed telemetry and a kernel health score to Console for rollouts.

Out of scope: Model-level quantization changes and kernel source changes (handled by the infra/kernel teams). This ticket focuses on orchestration, probing, gating, and runtime policy enforcement.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime can run a non-blocking microbench that validates per-GPU v3 workspace allocation and verifies a target latency band without blocking traffic
Automatic fallback to v2 kernels occurs for GPUs where microbench fails or where memory fragmentation causes OOMs
Canary rollout policy exists that promotes v3 on a per-GPU, per-model basis only after successful microbench and output-stability checks
Console shows kernel health score, microbench pass/fail, and first-token latency delta for canary hosts
No regressions in 95th/99th first-token latency for customer-facing canaries compared to baseline (within configured tolerance)
Rollout can be aborted/rolled back via existing rollout control in Console with no customer request loss
tasks: Design runtime shim API for kernel probe, health score, and policy enforcement (owner: Diego)
Implement microbench harness that runs quickly at GPU allocation and writes health to local cache (owner: Priya)
Add non-blocking warmup sequence that issues small prefix-only requests to pre-populate KV cache (owner: Victor)
Integrate fallback logic into kernel chooser: prefer v3 only after health pass, otherwise route to v2 (owner: Diego)
Emit telemetry events and expose kernel health metrics in Console (owner: Observability)
Create canary release orchestration: config flags, rollout gates, and automatic rollback triggers (owner: SRE)
Regression test suite: synthetic workloads (long sequence, cold cache, high concurrency) and compare to baseline (owner: QA)
Run phased canary on internal traffic, then external low-traffic customers, monitor for 48h before broader promotion (owner: PM)
Document behavior and troubleshooting steps in runtime runbook (owner: Diego)
Follow-up: schedule kernel team sync for microbench interpretation and potential upstream patch requests (owner: Amina)
Create GitHub PR(s) with implementation + unit/integration tests and link here
progress_updates: 2025-11-18: Ticket created after multiple post-deploy regressions reported in nightly canaries. Collected sample traces and heap snapshots from affected hosts.
2025-11-20: Reproduced increased first-token latency locally with an isolated long-seq workload; identified correlation with workspace reservation path in v3 allocator.
2025-11-24: Design review completed. Decided on non-blocking microbench + staged gate approach instead of global feature toggle to minimize blast radius.
2025-11-28: Microbench prototype implemented (alloc + tiny attention run), passes on 4/5 internal GPU variants; failing case tied to fragmented memory on older driver build.
2025-12-01: Fallback chooser integrated in local runtime. Added initial telemetry events. Beginning CI integration tests for synthetic workloads.
decisions: Use microbench at GPU allocation time rather than per-request probing to keep overhead low
Warmup sequence must be non-blocking and best-effort — it should not delay request processing
Health score combines: microbench pass/fail, short-term latency delta, and successful workspace allocations
Fallback to v2 is preferred over retrying v3 for the first N requests to avoid customer-visible tail latency spikes
Canary policy will be per-GPU and per-model variant to avoid cross-tenant impact
notes_for_oncall: If a canary reports repeated microbench failures, mark host as degraded and migrate traffic off GPU; escalate to kernel team if OOM patterns persist. Use rollout abort in Console to immediately revert promotional steps.
